channel_a.reasoning: Re-derived from evidence, and it moves. Two separate problems with the existing Substantive / Explicit attribution coding. (a) ATTRIBUTION. 'Explicit attribution' requires that THE COMPANY publicly connects its response to the finding or evaluator. Anthropic has published nothing connecting itself to this work. I searched its newsroom, research index, alignment blog, transparency hub, the Opus 5 card, the Mythos Preview card and the Fable 5 & Mythos 5 card, and the August 2026 Risk Report - the last four downloaded as PDFs and searched as full text. The link is asserted only by the evaluator. That is the definition of 'No explicit attribution', so Explicit attribution is wrong on the face of the rulebook regardless of what happens to Action Level. (b) ACTION LEVEL. The rulebook's admissibility rule is that only the company's own primary document counts; read at its strictest that forces None. But the rulebook also defines Partial as 'an action claimed but unverifiable', and here a dated, published record from the evaluator states that Anthropic iterated the monitor across successive versions and adopted AISI's best attacks into its own Mythos Preview testing. Coding None would force the attribution value 'No response located', which would be factually false. Partial is additionally supported on the merits: AISI states it 'found vulnerabilities in EVERY monitor version we tested', so on the evaluator's own account the remediation is incomplete - squarely 'interim, limited or incomplete action'. The Risk Report near-miss cuts the same way. Anthropic does document a monitor improvement cycle, but credits METR and internal red-teamers, with a coverage date eight days before the finding. So the underlying activity is real and corroborated in kind, while the specific attribution to UK AISI's Control Red Team is verifiable nowhere but in AISI's own post. Both prongs of the Partial definition are met -> Action Level = Partial, Attribution = No explicit attribution.
